chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:
I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام when ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī entered upon him, and with him were some people from his companions.
So he said: “Tell me, when two men are found in one covering.” He said to him: “ʿAlī عليه السلام, when he found two men in one covering, would administer the hadd punishment to them.”

Then ʿAbbād said: “You told me: one lash less.” So he repeated to him the mention of the hadd, until he repeated that to him several times, then he said: “One lash less.” Then the people present wrote down that hadith at that time.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, before whom the discussion took place
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment applied in this case
key_terms.عَبَّادٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ: the questioner who asked the Imam about the ruling
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose judicial practice is cited as precedent
key_terms.غَيْرَ سَوْطٍ: one lash less, indicating a punishment short of the complete number
key_terms.لِحَافٍ: a shared covering or blanket under which the two men were found

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on two men found in one covering?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal discussion before Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding the ruling on two men found under one covering. It attributes to Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام the application of a hadd punishment in such a case, with clarification that it was one lash less than the full hadd. The report is significant for Shia jurisprudence concerning sexual misconduct and penal rulings.
